A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same EndoCoT research work. All 23 pages in each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original EndoCoT benchmark results, ablations, inference-time scaling measurements, and qualitative studies in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons in Table 1 and supplementary analyses in Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same iterative thought guidance, terminal thought grounding, losses, joint LoRA adaptation, two-stage training, and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover Maze, TSP, Sudoku, VSP and larger-grid VSP, alongside image editing and generalization across maze sizes, fonts, and resolutions. The Figure 1 correction introduces no new task or scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain ThinkGen, ChronoEdit, Qwen3-VL-8B and its training variants, Qwen-Image-Edit-2511, and DiffThinker. The newly cited related work is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The zero-shot, task-specific, and unified settings, dataset sizes, rendering resolution, training settings, metrics, and reasoning-budget evaluations are unchanged, including the appendix protocols.

E4.justification: Figure 1(b) locally revises the qualitative evidence for maze-size generalization: the EndoCoT Standard Size panel changes from a Sudoku image to a maze solution. The analytical question, other case studies, ablations, and appendix robustness analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting. Neither reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: The displayed EndoCoT standard-size maze result in Figure 1(b) is corrected from a Sudoku image to a maze solution. Numerical results remain unchanged, including Table 1's task-specific averages of 92.1% for EndoCoT and 83.8% for DiffThinker; no performance gain between versions is established.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(13), the latent-state and loss formulations, and the appendix dataset-generation algorithms are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about endogenous iterative reasoning, inference-time scaling, benchmark advantages, and progressive image editing.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and interpretations remain unchanged. Both versions acknowledge manual selection of reasoning depth and dependence on high-quality intermediate supervision, and retain the same appendix observations about training and semantic supervision.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same code link, dataset-generation instructions, editing-data pipeline, and Table 7 configuration, including LoRA rank 32, learning rate 0.0001, and five training epochs.

R1.justification: v4 adds Rotstein et al., Pathways on the Image Manifold: Image Editing via Video Generation, as reference 23 in Section 2's existing Thinking with Video discussion. Other works are retained under shifted reference numbers; the novelty positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: The date and arXiv version header are updated, and citations are renumbered following the added reference. The prose, terminology, and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1(b) replaces the misplaced Sudoku panel with a maze solution, with slight figure and surrounding layout adjustments. The bibliography also reflows; other figure and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 fixes the conspicuous task-image mismatch in Figure 1(b), making the maze comparison clearer and internally consistent, and modestly expands related-work attribution. These are limited improvements in presentation and completeness; methods, quantitative evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged.
